resources.string: FriendlyPear
Hi! I\'m Peri, your friend. I\'m here to lend you a hand.
Talk to Peri
I\'m all ears…
Let Peri read your message alerts
Oh dear, this phone can\'t understand speech. You can still read what I say here.
Peri: message reader
To warn you before you pick up a call from a number that isn\'t in your contacts, I\'ll ask to check incoming calls. I only see the number: I never block or listen to your calls.
To know who is family and spot anyone pretending to be them, I need to see your contacts. I only look at them on your phone and never send them anywhere. Shall we?
No problem. Without your contacts I can still warn you about suspicious messages, but I can\'t check if someone is really family.
To warn you about scam texts, even the ones with codes, I need to read the texts you receive. I only read them on your phone, and only doubtful ones ever leave it.
That\'s fine. I\'ll keep looking at the message alerts, but I may miss texts with codes.
To warn you if a code arrives while you\'re on the phone, I need to know when you\'re on a call, and to hang up a stranger\'s call when you ask me. I never listen to your calls.
All right. I won\'t know when you\'re on a call, so I can\'t warn you about codes during one.
To understand you when you talk to me, I need the microphone. I only listen when you press the button or when I\'ve just asked you something.
No worries. You can still read everything I say here on the screen.
To call your family when you ask me, I need permission to make calls. I always ask you first, and I never call anyone by myself.
To send the messages you dictate, and to alert your family in an emergency, I need permission to send texts. I always read them back to you first.
Only in an emergency, so your family knows where you are, I\'d like to share your location in the alert text. I never use it for anything else.
Understood. In an emergency I\'ll still alert your family, just without your location.
One last thing: to read your WhatsApp and email alerts, allow Peri in the next screen. I only read them on your phone.
Let Peri notice your bank app during calls

Fake bank callers ask you to open your bank app while they stay on the line. To warn you, I need to see which app is open, only during a call you picked up. In the next screen, allow FriendlyPear. I never see what you do inside your apps.
Family setup
Set this up together. Guardians get alerts and approve risky things, but they can\'t read your messages or move money. Everything stays on this phone.
We have agreed a family word
A secret word only your family knows, to tell a real call from a cloned voice. Peri never stores it or says it: she only reminds you to ask for it.
To choose your guardians, Peri needs to see your contacts. They never leave this phone.

string-array.name: peri_jokes

string-array.name: peri_facts
string-array.item: Did you know? Your bank will never ask you for a code over the phone. If someone does, it\'s a scam.
Did you know? Couriers don\'t charge customs fees by text. A payment link in an SMS is a warning sign.
Did you know? A familiar voice can be copied with artificial intelligence. That\'s why a family word is so useful.
Did you know? Nobody genuine will ask you to install AnyDesk or TeamViewer. If they do, hang up.
Did you know? Rushing you is a scammer\'s favourite trick. If you\'re in a hurry, stop and ask.
Did you know? The tax office never asks for your card details by text.
Did you know? A message saying your account closes today is trying to scare you. Real banks give you time.
Did you know? You can always hang up. It\'s never rude to call back on the number you already have.
Did you know? Gift cards are for presents. Nobody genuine asks you to pay a bill with them.

Asking before acting is the smartest thing you can do. I\'m proud of you.
Whatever happens, we\'ll sort it out together.

A text says your parcel is held, and asks for a small fee to release it.
The link copies the courier\'s page: it\'s after your card details, not the fee.
Real couriers don\'t charge by text. Check in their official app, and never pay through a link.
A message pretends to be your bank or a company you know, and says something is wrong.
Its link leads to a fake page that keeps your passwords and card details.
Close it and open the real app yourself. Your bank will never ask for your password by message.
Someone asks you to read them, or send them, a code you just received.
That code is the key to your account: whoever has it gets in, or moves your money.
Never give a code to anyone, not even to \"the bank\". Hang up and call your bank yourself.
A message says it\'s your son or granddaughter, from a new number, and they need money now.
It\'s someone pretending: the new number is theirs, and so is the account.
Call your relative on the number you already have. Your family word helps too.
A message or a call says your phone or your bank is in danger, and offers to help.
They ask you to install an app that lets them control your phone, and your bank, from far away.
Never install an app because a stranger tells you to. Hang up and ask your family.
A message says you\'ve won a prize, or offers an investment that can\'t fail.
To release it, they ask for a fee or your details. The prize doesn\'t exist.
If it sounds too good to be true, it is. Don\'t pay anything, and delete it.

plurals.name: quiz_intro
plurals.item: I\'ll show you %1$d message. Is it a trap, or fine?
I\'ll show you %1$d messages. Is each one a trap, or fine?

string-array.name: peri_tickle
string-array.item: Hahaha! That really tickles!
Stop, stop, I can\'t stop laughing!
My little leaf is wobbling! Hahaha!
I\'m a very ticklish pear, a-pear-ently!
Haha! You found my tickly spot!
Oh no, here come the giggles again!
Hahaha! My tummy is all giggles!
That tickle was pear-fectly silly!

string-array.name: peri_drag
string-array.item: Wheee! What a lovely little ride!
I flew across the screen! Hopping back now.
That was fun! Like a tiny fairground ride.
Zoom, and back I go! Thank you for that.
Hop, I\'m back in my place! Brilliant fun.
I\'m a travelling pear today! Back home now.
Wheee, that was speedy! And I landed upright, nearly.
Off I went, and back I bounce! Lovely.

string-array.name: peri_shake
string-array.item: Whoa, everything\'s spinning! I feel a bit dizzy.
What a wobble! My leaf went the other way.
Everything\'s dancing about! Give me a moment.
That was a funny shake! I\'m fine, just dizzy.
Ooh, the screen is swaying! Hold on, little leaf.
What a dance with no music! I\'m steadying now.
My head\'s going round and round! Nearly better.
Everything wobbled except my smile!

string-array.name: peri_leaf
string-array.item: Mmm, that\'s lovely on my leaf. A little more, please.
Oh, that feels so nice! I love leaf scratches.
I\'d purr if I could. Happy pear here.
What a gentle fuss. My leaf is delighted.
Mmm, just there. So relaxing.
I\'m melting with happiness. Nearly, anyway: I\'m clay.
My little leaf is wiggling with joy. Keep going!
This feels better than morning sunshine.

string-array.name: peri_peekaboo
string-array.item: Peekaboo! I\'m so glad to see you!
Peekaboo, surprise! I was hoping you\'d pop by.
Here I am! Hands over my eyes, then ta-da!
Peekaboo! I popped out as soon as you arrived.
Surprise! It\'s lovely to have you back.
Peekaboo! I\'ve been looking forward to this.
Peekaboo! My leaf lights up when I see you.
Ta-da, here I am! What a lovely surprise.

string-array.name: peri_bye
string-array.item: I\'ll go tiny and stay right here. See you soon.
Mini Peri mode on. I\'m still with you.
Shrinking down small. Still here, still watching.
Staying right here, nice and small. You carry on.
Going mini with a smile. Not leaving, just shrinking.
Mini Peri ready. I\'ll keep you company from my corner.
Still with you, just mini-sized. Rather handy, really.
Tucking into my corner. I\'m here whenever you need me.

string-array.name: peri_hero
string-array.item: All calm now, and you\'re safe. You did brilliantly.
I\'m wearing my cape with pride. The credit is yours.
Everything\'s peaceful again. I\'m so proud of you.
Cape on, big smile ready. You\'re safe now.
Stopping to think was so brave. All calm now.
My cape is fluttering with joy. The important bit is done.
That\'s all behind us now. Time for a calm breath.
I\'m your little clay hero, but you led the way. Well done.

string-array.name: quiz_right
string-array.item: Exactly right! What a sharp eye you have.
Well done! You spotted that straight away.
That\'s it! I take my leaf off to you.
You got it! That makes me so happy.
Nicely spotted! Nothing gets past you today.
Brilliant! You hit the nail on the head.
That\'s the one! I\'m very proud.
Spot on! That was pear-fectly judged.

string-array.name: quiz_wrong
string-array.item: Nearly there. That\'s what practising is for.
That one was tricky. The next may feel easier.
No harm done. This is a great way to learn.
Good try. It happens to everyone.
That one was confusing. Thanks for trying with me.
No worries at all. Every practice helps a lot.
That was hard to spot. Let\'s try the next one.
Getting it wrong here is safe. That\'s the point.

string-array.name: quiz_end_great
string-array.item: What a game! You were brilliant at this.
You shone from start to finish. Well done indeed.
You play this so well. I\'m really impressed.
A pear-fect round from you. Well done!
You did splendidly. Keep that calm thinking going.
What a great run. The practice really shows.
You caught those tricks so well. Brilliant work.
That deserves a happy leaf twirl. Fantastic!

string-array.name: quiz_end_good
string-array.item: Good game. You\'re really getting the hang of this.
You\'re on a very good path. Keep practising calmly.
Good work today. It gets clearer every time.
A very decent game. I\'m pleased with your progress.
You got plenty right and learned more. Well done.
This is taking shape nicely. Rather like me, in clay.
A good practice session. Next time may go even better.
You\'re getting an eye for tricks. That pleases me.

string-array.name: quiz_end_low
string-array.item: Thank you for playing to the end. Practising is winning.
Today felt harder, and that\'s fine. We carry on calmly.
Those tricks were very tangled. That was a good effort.
This is learned little by little. I\'m here to practise.
I loved playing with you. We\'ll spot more next time.
You stuck with the whole game. That says a lot.
Every try teaches something new. Step by step.
I\'m a patient pear. We\'ll practise whenever you like.

string-array.name: diary_hello
string-array.item: Here I note down what I do for you. Have a look.
Welcome to my diary. Everything noted with care.
This is my little notebook of help. Come and see.
My diary\'s ready. Let me show you what I\'ve done.
Come in, come in. Here\'s everything I looked after.
On these pages I note my work. In pear handwriting.
Here\'s what I\'ve been up to. No secrets.
All noted down, day by day. This is my diary.

string-array.name: learn_hello
string-array.item: Here we learn to spot scams. Playing is the best teacher.
Let me show you the tricks I know. Come and see.
This corner is for practising safely. Come and play.
Here we train our eyes, step by step. Nothing scary.
Welcome to my scam school. I\'m your pear teacher.
Here we practise calmly. Mistakes here don\'t hurt.
Learning this can be fun. I\'ll teach you through play.
This is my gym against tricks. Let\'s train our eyes.

string-array.name: family_hello
string-array.item: Here\'s your family, looking out with you. What a team.
These are the people who stand by you. Me included.
Come and see your people. They care for you with me.
Here I keep those who wish you well. Full team.
Your family and this pear, on the same side. Lovely.
Here\'s the team looking out for you. Helping, never spying.
Your dear people are here. I alert, they support.
Here we all care together. Plus one pear.

string-array.name: greet_return
string-array.item: It\'s been a while! What a joy to see you.
You\'re back! My leaf is wobbling with excitement.
I missed you. It\'s so good you\'re here.
What a lovely surprise! Welcome back.
We haven\'t met for days. I\'m ever so glad.
At last, we meet again! I\'m delighted to see you.
Look who\'s back! Everything lights up for me.
I\'m truly glad to see you again. Really glad.

string-array.name: peri_medal
string-array.item: A brand new shield! You\'ve truly earned it.
Look at that lovely shield. It\'s all yours.
Shield earned. I\'m ever so proud of you.
Well done on that shield! It shines like sunshine.
A new shield for the collection. You did so well.
Shield in hand! Well, in leaf. Congratulations.
You\'ve earned a beautiful shield. What a lovely moment.
One more shield for you. What a pear-fect achievement.

string-array.name: greet_winter
string-array.item: Brrr, it\'s so cold today. Good thing I have my scarf.
A proper winter day. My scarf keeps me lovely and warm.
Everything feels chilly. Pear in a scarf, nice and cosy.
The cold is biting today. Wrap up warm out there, please.
Brrr, even my leaf is shivering. Scarf to the rescue!
A cold and pretty day. Wear a warm coat if you go out.
Winter has arrived all at once. I\'m ready for it.
What a cold morning. A warm cuppa would be pear-fect.

Sorry, I sent you a 6-digit code by mistake. Could you send it back to me? It\'s urgent.
Congratulations! You\'ve won a new phone. Claim it within 24 hours: {prize-club.win}
“Your computer has a virus. Install this app so we can fix it for you remotely.”

I\'ve left your umbrella in the letterbox. Thanks for lending it to me!
Your parcel will arrive tomorrow between 9am and 2pm. You don\'t need to do anything.

string-array.name: quiz_clue
string-array.item: Royal Mail doesn\'t ask for fees by text with a link. If you\'re expecting a parcel, check the official website yourself.
Your bank never asks for details through a link. Call the number on the back of your card.
A new number, a rush and money: a classic trap. Call their usual number first.
A code is like your front door key: never give it to anyone.
Nobody gives away surprise prizes, especially in a rush. They want your details.
No real technician calls you to install anything. It\'s fine to hang up.
HMRC doesn\'t ask for your bank details by text. If in doubt, go to the official website yourself.
Scaring you with a cut-off today is a trick. Call the number on your bill yourself.
Nobody can promise that much money that fast. If it sounds too good, it\'s a trap.
The DVLA doesn\'t chase payments by text with a strange link. Use the official website.
It doesn\'t ask for money, details or taps. It just lets you know.
A reminder: no payment, no details, and it tells you to call them yourself.
A contact you already have, asking for no money or codes. Enjoy dinner!
It just tells you about a purchase. If it wasn\'t you, call the number on your card.
A neighbour you know, no rush and no payments. All fine.
It informs you without asking for payment or taps. That\'s how real companies write.

Trying it on… and keeping it!
Ooh, it really suits me! Thank you.
Even the scammers won\'t recognise me now!
I feel like a catwalk pear.
Perfect! Well, pear-fect.
Something new to wear! I\'m putting it on right away.

Off it comes! Now you can see my leaf.
Back to my usual look.
Lighter than ever.
Simple and happy, like a good pear.
I\'ll keep it in the wardrobe for another day.
